extracted.intended_audience: patent litigators, appellate judges, and patent law practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Federal Circuit guidance on §101 patent-eligibility (Alice two-step focus/inventive-concept analysis) and on awarding damages (including extraterritoriality under WesternGeco, reasonable-royalty calculation, apportionment, and causation). Intended to govern analysis in patent litigation and appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alice Step One — focus of the claimed advance
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider 'the focus of the claimed advance over the prior art' to determine whether the claims are directed to an abstract idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the focus is on receipt and display of information (even of a particular type) and use of that information to engage in a fundamental economic practice, that focus can be an abstract idea (e.g., receipt/display of bids and offers to assist trading). Compare whether the claim improves computers or merely arranges information. See IBG II and related precedents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alice Step Two — inventive concept requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An inventive concept is required to transform a claim directed to an abstract idea into eligible subject matter; the abstract idea itself cannot supply the inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claim elements, individually and as an ordered combination, must add something significantly more than the abstract idea. Mere use of preexisting computers or routine programming does not supply an inventive concept. Courts treat routine data gathering and conventional display techniques as not adding an inventive concept (e.g., receiving market information and displaying indicators along a scaled price axis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvement in computer functionality required (negative test)
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim must show an improvement in computer functionality to avoid being merely an automation of a manual process using generic computers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mere automation of manual processes using generic computers is not an improvement; arranging information along an axis does not improve computer functioning or solve a technological problem. Look for language in the specification that calls for more than preexisting computers and known programming techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess claim elements both individually and as an ordered combination
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating inventive concept, consider whether the specific claim elements, individually and as an ordered combination, add the necessary inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if claim elements make particular choices among abstract ideas involving information and ordering, those choices alone do not suffice unless they amount to something significantly more that transforms the abstract idea into eligible subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of precedent and precedential weight
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-precedential decisions are not binding and cannot be treated as controlling authority for eligibility or other issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on non-precedential decisions as binding law; differences in claims, specifications, or patents can be a sufficient basis to distinguish them. Precedential decisions and a body of case law applying Alice should be followed where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: WesternGeco framework governs extraterritorial damages under §284
rubrics_metrics.description: For determining whether patent damages may be awarded based on foreign conduct, apply the Supreme Court's WesternGeco extraterritoriality framework rather than the earlier Power Integrations analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WesternGeco's two-step framework (presumption against extraterritoriality; if not rebutted, determine whether the case involves a domestic application by identifying the statute's focus) now governs damages analysis under §284. Courts should proceed under WesternGeco in future cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-step extraterritoriality inquiry (WesternGeco)
rubrics_metrics.description: First ask whether the presumption against extraterritoriality is rebutted; second, if not, determine whether the case involves a domestic application of the statute by identifying the statute's focus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifying the statute's 'focus' means finding the object of its solicitude (conduct it regulates, parties/interests it seeks to protect). For §284, WesternGeco began with §284 and concluded the statutory focus is 'the infringement.' Courts then examine the statutory provision defining the infringement at issue (e.g., §271 provisions) to decide if the conduct relevant to that focus is domestic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory focus for §284 is 'the infringement'
rubrics_metrics.description: In the WesternGeco analysis, the relevant focus of §284 (damages) is 'the infringement', so the inquiry asks whether the conduct relevant to that infringement is domestic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because §284's purpose is to afford complete compensation for 'the infringement,' courts identify which statutory provision defines the infringement being alleged (e.g., §271(f)(2) or §271(a)) and evaluate whether that provision's focus is domestic conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: WesternGeco applies to §271(a) and to reasonable-royalty awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The WesternGeco framework applies not only to §271(f) and lost-profits awards but also to §271(a) infringement and to reasonable-royalty awards under §284.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply WesternGeco by examining the particular acts alleged to constitute infringement under the specific statutory provision to determine whether those acts focus on domestic conduct. When applying to reasonable royalties, account for conceptual and evidentiary differences between lost-profits and reasonable-royalty measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypothetical negotiation for reasonable-royalty calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the common hypothetical-negotiation approach to calculate a reasonable royalty: attempt to ascertain the royalty the parties would have agreed to just before infringement began.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The hypothetical negotiation should identify the incremental value of the claimed technology over noninfringing alternatives and determine how that gain would be shared. Courts and juries consider established authorities (Lucent, Asetek, VLSI, Carnegie Mellon, AstraZeneca) and jury instructions on the hypothetical negotiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Royalty base limited to acts constituting infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: The royalty base for reasonable-royalty damages cannot include activities that do not constitute patent infringement; damages are limited to amounts adequate to compensate for the infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude noninfringing activities from the royalty base; recover damages only for infringing acts after issuance of the patent. Examples include excluding pre-issuance activities and unrelated product value when calculating the royalty base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apportionment — royalty must reflect value of patented technology
rubrics_metrics.description: The bottom-line royalty must be apportioned to the value of the patented technology by separating out and excluding other value in economic products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and remove value attributable to nonpatented features or other factors to ensure the royalty compensates only for the patented invention's contribution. Use evidence to establish the incremental value of the patented feature over alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causation requirement for damages under §284
rubrics_metrics.description: Damages under §284 require a causation showing (at least but-for causation) linking the infringement to the patentee's losses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WesternGeco recognized that §284's directive to provide 'complete compensation' entails a causation element (e.g., 'how much the Patent Holder suffered by the infringement' and the 'difference between [its] condition after the infringement, and what [it] would have been if the infringement had not occurred'). The court left open the extent to which doctrines such as proximate cause might further limit damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign conduct may be incidental to domestic infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign events that contribute to the patentee's loss may be merely incidental to the infringement and not have primacy for extraterritoriality analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if foreign conduct contributes to injury abroad (e.g., foreign assembly or sales), the infringement can remain domestic for extraterritoriality analysis if the statutory focus is domestic (as WesternGeco held for §271(f)(2)). Courts should assess whether overseas events are 'incidental' rather than the focus of the statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary standard for expert exclusion and appellate review
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion of expert evidence under Federal Rule of Evidence 702 is reviewed under the standards of the pertinent regional circuit (here, Seventh Circuit abuse-of-discretion); interpretations of patent law underlying exclusion are reviewed de novo by the Federal Circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a district court excludes expert testimony, appellate courts consider whether the exclusion constituted an abuse of discretion (regional standard). If the exclusion rests on an interpretation of patent law, the Federal Circuit applies its own law and reviews that legal interpretation without deference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory text can rebut presumption against extraterritoriality
rubrics_metrics.description: If a statute clearly indicates extraterritorial application (e.g., by expressly covering importation), that can rebut the presumption against extraterritoriality at step one of the WesternGeco framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, §271(a) expressly covers importing into the United States; if importing is characterized as extraterritorial, the statute's express language may constitute a clear indication of extraterritorial application, changing the analysis under WesternGeco.
